newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL shares close lower, blue chips off lows.
newsitem.headline: KL shares close lower, blue chips off lows.

text.p: Malaysian shares closed broadly lower on thin volume and a lack of investor interest, dealers and analysts said.

The Composite Index of 100 large-capitalised stocks ended 5.28 points lower to 1,197.78, while the small-cap Second Board index was off 6.66 points to 533.65. The Composite Index had dropped to 1,194.32 earlier in the afternoon.
"There are not going to be any major movements until next year," said Kenny Yee, senior investment analyst at Nikko Advisory Services in Kuala Lumpur.
Volume stood at 112 million shares, valued at 803 million ringgit. Losers overwhelmed gainers 418 to 149, with 150 stocks remaining unchanged.
Affin Holdings was up 15 cents to 6.95 ringgit. The company had received approval from the Ministry of Finance to establish a stockbroking firm on Friday.
"There are all of three people on our dealing room floor in Singapore," said an analyst at a Kuala Lumpur equities research house.
Bus maker Taiping Super closed at 12 ringgit after debuting at 8.50 ringgit on an offer price of 2.50 ringgit.
